cases.name: pool-without-a-name-or-a-count
cases.description: A pool is read by name and sized by count; without either there is nothing to reference and nothing to hand out.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><pool><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence></pool></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: pool-count-that-is-not-a-number-of-members
cases.description: A pool of zero has no member to hand out, and a count that is not a whole number is not a size at all.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="D" count="0"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence></pool></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-block-cannot-live-inside-a-pool
cases.description: A pool has no output of its own — it is a table other columns read — so <block> and the fixtures, which describe a FILE, mean nothing inside one. A nested <pool> is refused for a different reason: a pool stays a flat table, and one pool pointing at another says the same thing without making every later feature ask at which depth it applies.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="D" count="3"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence><block><line><data>no</data></line></block></pool></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-reference-to-a-pool-that-is-not-declared
cases.description: The generator names the pool it draws from, so a name that is not a declared pool has nothing behind it. Reported at the reference, with the declared pools listed. The TDC193 beside it is the knock-on: with no pool there are no fields for R either.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="D" count="3"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.c}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-filter-that-reads-a-field-the-pool-has-not-got
cases.description: A name written Pool.field says exactly what it means, so a field the pool does not declare is a certain mistake. An UNQUALIFIED unknown name is deliberately NOT reported: the expression language reads a bare word as a string literal, which is how filter="c == North" says "northern only".
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="D" count="3"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="D" filter="D.zzz == c"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.c}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-reference-read-without-a-field
cases.description: A reference draws a whole MEMBER, so it has no single value to print. Without this check the reference reached the output as literal text — a name that exists, resolves to nothing, and says nothing.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="D" count="3"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="D"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-name-that-is-both-a-pool-field-and-a-column
cases.description: filter= is evaluated in two scopes at once — the candidate's fields and the row's columns — so a name in both is not decidable. Qualifying one side does not repair it: the other bare name still reads as the field, and the test would compare a value with itself.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="D" count="3"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="D" filter="c == c"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.c}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-too-large-to-keep-in-memory
cases.description: A pool is held in memory for the whole run — measured at about 320 bytes a member with four fields, so a million members cost a third of a gigabyte before the first row. Above the ceiling it is refused; above 100,000 it is a warning (TDC234). Both messages name the likelier mistake: a count typed onto the wrong tag.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="D" count="2000000"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="D"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.c}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-large-enough-to-be-worth-noticing
cases.description: The warning half of the ceiling: 200,000 members work and cost about 60 MB for the whole run. It is a warning because the config is correct — it is just worth being deliberate about.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="D" count="200000"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="D"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.c}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-that-draws-from-a-pool-declared-below
cases.description: Pools are built in the order they are written, so a member may only draw from a pool ABOVE it. Without this the config validated and produced a member with no fields, and the complaint surfaced far away as "not a field of R" — blaming the line that reads for a mistake made in the declaration.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="p" local="en"><pool name="D" count="2"><sequence name="a"><gen type="text" value="x,y"/></sequence><sequence name="at"><gen type="pool" value="C"/></sequence></pool><pool name="C" count="2"><sequence name="k"><gen type="text" value="n,s"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="D"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.a}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-that-draws-from-itself
cases.description: A pool is built before its own members exist, so there is nothing to draw. The same code as the forward reference, because it is the same rule: only the pools above.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="p" local="en"><pool name="D" count="2"><sequence name="a"><gen type="text" value="x,y"/></sequence><sequence name="me"><gen type="pool" value="D"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="D"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.a}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-carries-an-attribute-the-engine-does-not-read
cases.description: A <pool> is a closed tag like every other, so an attribute it does not read has to be reported rather than ignored. seed= is the one that invites the mistake: a pool DOES have its own seed, derived as `<seed>#pool:<name>`, and it is not settable — so writing it silently changed nothing at all.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="P" count="2" seed="own"><sequence name="a"><gen type="text" value="x,y"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="P"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.a}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: two-pools-under-one-name
cases.description: The second pool quietly replaced the first, and the only sign was a TDC193 in the block about a field that "does not exist" — sending the reader to look in the wrong place entirely. <sequence> has said this since TDC032; a pool is a declaration too.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="P" count="2"><sequence name="f"><gen type="text" value="f1,f2"/></sequence></pool><pool name="P" count="2"><sequence name="g"><gen type="text" value="g1,g2"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="c"><gen type="pool" value="P"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{c.g}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-nobody-draws-from
cases.description: A pool is built in full before the first row and held for the whole run, so one nothing reads is paid for and thrown away. A warning, not an error, on the same reasoning as TDC234: every row is exactly what it would have been.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="D" count="3"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence></pool></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-filter-comparing-two-lists-that-do-not-overlap
cases.description: The member's field and the column each draw from a list the config writes down, and the two do not meet — so the filter narrows every row to no member at all, not merely some. Only DISJOINT lists are reported: a value that is merely rare is a refusal waiting for the row that draws it, and percent="100,0" may never draw it.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="D" count="3"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="W"><gen type="text" value="Y,Z"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="D" filter="c == W"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.c}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-filter-against-a-word-no-member-holds
cases.description: A bare word is a literal — that is how filter="c == North" says northern only — so it is a list of exactly one value, and the same disjointness decides it. This is the typo TDC227 was cancelled for: it is not reported as an unknown name, it is reported as a comparison nothing can satisfy.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="D" count="3"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="D" filter="c == North"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.c}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-filter-whose-lists-do-overlap
cases.description: The half of the check that must never fire: the lists meet, so some member matches and nothing is said.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="D" count="3"><sequence name="c"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="W"><gen type="text" value="A,Z"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="D" filter="c == W"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.c}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: if-on-a-pool-reference-is-refused
cases.description: A `<gen>` carrying `if=` becomes a conditional branch, and the pool resolver only recognises a plain `<gen type="pool">`. So the reference registered no `Ref.field` columns at all and `${{Ref.name}}` reached the output as its own literal text — on EVERY row, including the ones the condition selected — from a config `check` had called valid. Refused rather than implemented: leaving a row without a member is what `parent=` already does, and a conditional reference would have to answer what `${{Ref.field}}` means on a row that took the other branch.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="s"><pool name="P" count="2"><sequence name="n"><gen type="text" value="a,b"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="K"><gen type="text" value="y,n"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen if="K == y" type="pool" value="P"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.n}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-that-draws-from-one-declared-below-it
cases.description: Pools are built in declaration order, so a pool can only read the pools above it — which is also why a cycle between pools cannot be written down. Added when the documentation checker found the message quoted on the pools page with no case behind it.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><pool name="Doctors" count="2"><sequence name="at"><gen type="pool" value="Clinics"/></sequence></pool><pool name="Clinics" count="2"><sequence name="city"><gen type="text" value="N,S"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="X"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X.at}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: pool-member-if-reads-an-env-column
cases.description: A pool is built before any row exists, so a member's condition naming a run column is constant-false on every member — badge came out empty on every row while check called the config valid.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="clinic" local="en"><pool name="Doctors" count="6"><sequence name="name"><gen type="template" value="person.lastName"/></sequence><sequence name="badge"><gen type="text" value="B" if="Age >= 18"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="Age"><gen type="number" value="1..10"/></sequence><sequence name="Seen"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>badge=[${{Seen.badge}}]</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: pool-member-if-reads-a-sibling-field
cases.description: The other direction of the same scope: a member reads its pool's own fields, which the engine resolves, so this must not be refused.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="po" local="en"><pool name="Doctors" count="6"><sequence name="role"><gen type="text" value="surgeon,nurse"/></sequence><sequence name="scalpel"><gen type="text" value="yes" if="role == surgeon"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="Seen"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{Seen.role}} s[${{Seen.scalpel}}]</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: group-mixes-a-reference-with-an-ordinary-sequence
cases.description: A <distinct> over pool references compares WHICH MEMBER the row took; over ordinary sequences it compares the value. One group does one of the two — a record and a string have no field the comparison would be about. Accepted and silently inert before this.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="10" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="Doctors" count="4"><sequence name="name" uniq="true"><gen type="text" value="Adams,Brooks,Chase,Dunn"/></sequence></pool><distinct><sequence name="A"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors"/></sequence><sequence name="Plain"><gen type="text" value="Adams,Brooks"/></sequence></distinct></env><block><line><data>${{A.name}}|${{Plain}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: group-holds-references-to-two-different-pools
cases.description: A member of one pool is never a member of another, so the group would be satisfied without changing anything — the silent no-op the code path had all along, now named.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="10" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="Doctors" count="4"><sequence name="name" uniq="true"><gen type="text" value="Adams,Brooks,Chase,Dunn"/></sequence></pool><pool name="Wards" count="4"><sequence name="no" uniq="true"><gen type="text" value="101,102,103,104"/></sequence></pool><distinct><sequence name="A"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors"/></sequence><sequence name="W"><gen type="pool" value="Wards"/></sequence></distinct></env><block><line><data>${{A.name}}|${{W.no}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: group-puts-more-references-on-a-pool-than-it-has-members
cases.description: Three references cannot each take a different member of a pool of two. Provable before a row exists, so it is refused there rather than on the first row that cannot be satisfied.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="10" seed="s" local="en"><pool name="Doctors" count="2"><sequence name="name" uniq="true"><gen type="text" value="Adams,Brooks"/></sequence></pool><distinct><sequence name="A"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors"/></sequence><sequence name="C"><gen type="pool" value="Doctors"/></sequence></distinct></env><block><line><data>${{A.name}}|${{B.name}}|${{C.name}}</data></line></block></tdc>
